subject: Uptown Energy - price match playbook & runtime gap analysis
messages:
From: Hector Alvarez <hector.alvarez@uptown-energy.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@uptown-energy.com>
Date: Thu, 2 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: price match and runtime parity details

Marcus —

Thanks for the conversation earlier. We received a competing offer from a vendor who is willing to put a formal number on both unit pricing and a migration assistance package. Before we proceed to an internal approval loop, can Redwood provide a firm price match and confirm any runtime/throughput parity guarantees for our inference workload?

Quick facts:
- Expected baseline: ~12M tokens/month initially, scaling to 40–45M by Q4.
- Latency target (p95): <= 250ms for our 1k token avg inference case.
- Primary need: hosted API with an option to move to Dedicated in 2–3 months.

The competing offer includes a 30% discount vs. your current list, a 6-month migration credit of $60k, and an SLA credit clause if p95 exceeds 350ms more than twice in a month.

If Redwood can match on economics and provide an ops plan that demonstrates parity, procurement is willing to move quickly. I attached the competitor term summary for reference.

Thanks —
Hector Alvarez
Director of ML Platforms
Uptown Energy

Attachment: competitor_terms_summary.pdf (summary stub)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hector Alvarez <hector.alvarez@uptown-energy.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 2 May 2028 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: price match and runtime parity details

Hector —

Appreciate the level of detail and for sharing the competitor summary. We're confident we can present a competitive counterproposal, but I need to validate a few items so we match cleanly:

1) Volume and commit term you're comfortable with (12M/month baseline vs forecast).
2) Spike profile: any hourly/weekly burst patterns we should model for autoscale.
3) Which workloads require strict p95 <=250ms vs bulk batch?

We can do two things quickly:
- Fast internal econ check and a tailored term sheet.
- A short ops runbook showing how we'll achieve the p95 target (prefill cache, dedicated pool for critical routes).

Cc'ing Jordan to draft a commercial option and Grace to start a brief runtime gap analysis. We'll attach our preliminary numbers and an MMP (migration & match playbook) spreadsheet.

Can you confirm the commit term you're targeting (12 months / 24 months)?

Best,
Marcus Lin
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachment: none

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 2 May 2028 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Uptown price-match playbook (draft)

Team —

Quick notes after Hector's ask. I built a short economics/ops proposal (attached) and sketched three options we can offer:

Option A (aggressive match)
- 28% off list on hosted usage for first 12 months
- 6-month migration credit equivalent to $50k in bill credits
- 6-week dedicated capacity trial (no extra infra charge)
- SLA credit up to 10% monthly bill if p95 > 350ms more than twice in a 30-day period

Option B (balanced)
- 22% off list with a 24-month reserved commit at a discounted rate
- Migration professional services capped at $40k
- Faster onboarding with Redwood Optimize playbook

Option C (enterprise reserved)
- 18% off + fixed monthly dedicated capacity price (best long-term unit economics)
- On-call escalation and quarterly architecture reviews

Ops notes (Grace): initial read shows their 1k-token average inference will benefit from prefix caching and a small dedicated pool for hot traffic. We can demonstrate p95 parity in a 48–72 hour synthetic run if they agree to a short pilot.

Risks: the competitor's 30% ask is above our typical flexibility unless we ask for a stronger commit term or add migration/marketplace considerations. FinEdge (cc'd on their inbound) might expect a broker fee; factor that into the credit math.

I'll recommend presenting Option A as a time-limited counter if Hector wants a fast close, but we should be prepared to ask for a 12-month revenue commitment and a short exclusivity window for the migration credits.

Attachment: uptown_mmp_analysis.xlsx

Thanks —
Marcus

From: Hector Alvarez <hector.alvarez@uptown-energy.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@uptown-energy.com>, FinEdge Partners <sales@finedge.com>
Date: Fri, 3 May 2028 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Uptown - price match playbook & runtime gap analysis

Marcus / team —

Thanks for the quick follow. A few clarifications from procurement after internal review:

- They will accept a 12-month minimum commitment but want a larger concession if we cannot meet the 30% headline.
- Migration credit: $60k was their ask; $50k is close but procurement prefers $60k or an additional SLA credit wedge.
- SLA expectations: the competitor's clause includes automatic credits after two p95 breaches; Procurement wants a similar automatic remedy (not a discretionary SLA).

We are okay with a 48–72 hour pilot to validate p95 as long as that pilot data is accepted as gating the SLA. Also, is the 6-week dedicated trial a guaranteed window or subject to capacity?

Attaching procurement checklist (procurement_requirements.pdf).

Hector

Attachment: uptown_procurement_requirements.pdf

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hector Alvarez <hector.alvarez@uptown-energy.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, FinEdge Partners <sales@finedge.com>
Date: Sat, 4 May 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Uptown - price match playbook & runtime gap analysis

Hector —

Appreciate the transparency and the procurement checklist. We've run the numbers and can move quickly if Uptown is willing to accept a structured, milestone-based match rather than a single unconditional 30% headline. Proposed commercial offer (time-limited):

- Economics: 28% off list for months 1–12 on hosted usage, then 18% discount thereafter for the remainder of a 24-month term should Uptown sign a 24-month commitment.
- Migration assistance: $60k in bill credits (equal to your ask), applied across the first 3 billing cycles.
- Dedicated trial: guaranteed 4-week dedicated pool (pre-reserved capacity) within 30 days of SOW signature; if Uptown converts to Dedicated within 90 days, trial credit is applied to the committed spend.
- SLA: automatic credits up to 10% of monthly invoice if p95 exceeds 350ms more than twice in a 30-day window. The 48–72h synthetic pilot will be accepted as the baseline for SLA measurements.
- Condition: commit to a minimum 12-month revenue floor (we can flex the headline discount up to 28% only with the 24-month committed option).

We will send an updated term sheet (attached) and a DocuSign link for the term sheet + SOW. Please review and I'll set up a 30-minute call to finalize.

Best regards,
Jordan Blake
Commercial Lead, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-term-sheet-v2.pdf
DocuSign: https://docusign.net/Signing/?DocId=abc123-up-2028
